spread/plain: A plain autoencoder maps each input to one code: a single point.
spread/two: A variational autoencoder, or VAE, gives two numbers for every code dimension instead: a mean, written mu, the Greek letter mu, and a spread, sigma, the Greek letter sigma. Here sigma is a standard deviation, not the sigmoid. With a code of two dimensions, the encoder outputs four numbers.
spread/bell: Each pair describes a bell curve. Codes near the mean are likely, and the spread says how far they range: here one, give or take a half, and minus a half, give or take zero point two.
sample/eps: In training, the decoder does not get the mean. First draw noise from a standard normal, with mean zero and spread one. It is written epsilon, the Greek letter epsilon: here zero point four and minus one.
sample/z: Stretch it by the spread and shift it by the mean: z is mu plus sigma times epsilon. One, plus a half times zero point four, is one point two. Minus a half, plus zero point two times minus one, is minus zero point seven.
sample/why: Every step draws a fresh code near the mean, and the decoder has to rebuild the same input from each one. So a whole neighborhood of codes comes to decode alike.
sample/grad: The randomness sits in epsilon, which no weight sets. So backprop still reaches mu and sigma: z moves one for one with mu, and by epsilon times any change in sigma.
prior/drift: Left alone, training would shrink every spread toward zero, making codes exact again, and scatter the means wherever it liked, with gaps in between.
prior/term: So the loss gets an extra term for each code dimension: one half of mu squared, plus sigma squared, minus one, minus the log of sigma squared.
prior/zero: It is zero only when mu is zero and sigma is one: a standard normal. Move the mean away, or shrink or widen the spread, and it grows. So it pulls every input's bell toward that one.
prior/generate: With every code crowded into the same region, a fresh draw from a standard normal lands where the decoder knows what to do. Decode it, and out comes a new image.
